title: Operations facilities plan and Greener Homes loans
subtitle: Also: Smart Cities food and circular economy update, organics processing contract renewal, and CAO performance objectives.
overview: The committee recommended a revised plan for city operations buildings. A new transit and fleet facility would be designed at Watson Parkway South and Stone Road East, and other services would stay in renovated existing sites {{vote:m3}}. Staff gave no firm cost. Several councillors raised concerns about cost, debt capacity and timing alongside the Baker Street and South End recreation projects. Staff said costs would return through the budget process.

The committee also recommended delegating authority to staff to sign agreements for the Guelph Greener Homes Program {{vote:m4}}. The program offers zero-interest loans repaid through property taxes over ten years, with a launch targeted for the second quarter of 2023. A final program by-law is due back on February 28.

The committee recommended renewing the organics processing agreement with the Region of Waterloo and suspending its annual price adjustment {{vote:m2}}. It received the Smart Cities update, with federal funding ending in December 2023 and a plan for the future due by June {{vote:m1}}. The CAO also presented 2023 performance objectives, which needed no motion.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended continuing design of a transit and fleet facility at Watson Parkway South and Stone Road East, using existing municipal sites for other services, with funding to be sought through the multi-year budget.

The committee recommended giving the Deputy CAO of Infrastructure, Development and Enterprise, and the City Clerk and program manager for property owner agreements, authority to sign program agreements for the City.
The committee recommended renewing the green cart organics processing agreement for five years from October 14, 2023, and suspending the annual price index adjustment.
The committee received the report on the Our Food Future and Circular Opportunity Innovation Launchpad programs for information.

debate: On the operations facilities plan, several councillors said they were uneasy approving it without a cost. They noted the earlier concept was far larger and that ten renovation projects were now being added. Staff said detailed design must come first, and that cost estimates would appear in the multi-year budget.

Staff and the CAO argued the plan was needed for transit electrification. Existing sites lack space and electrical capacity, and federal infrastructure grant funding carries timing deadlines. One councillor said delay would add cost. Another asked for a separate discussion of timelines and costs before the budget.

A councillor questioned whether the city could deliver this alongside the Baker Street and South End recreation projects, and raised concern about debt capacity and development charges. Staff said added project management capacity and smaller renovation scale made delivery manageable.

On Greener Homes, councillors asked about equity for households that cannot pay up front, low-rise rental buildings and larger apartments, and buyers learning of an existing charge. Staff pointed to a partial up-front loan, a low-income rebate still being designed, and tax certificates that disclose the charge.

Delegates on the Smart Cities update praised the program's results but warned about sustaining food access work once federal funding ends. One suggested an office of food or a similar partnership model.
